title: Limit of accuracy
competency: Round numbers to a given accuracy and find the bounds of rounded values and of answers worked out from them.

keywords.def: Replacing a number by a simpler nearby value, such as 38,721 → 38,700 to the nearest hundred.
A digit after the decimal point. 3.17 is given to 2 decimal places (2 d.p.).
The digits of a number counted from the first non-zero digit. 0.0062 has 2 significant figures.
The smallest value a number could have had before it was rounded.
The value just above the largest a number could have had before rounding. The number is always less than it.

ideas.name: Rounding, decimal places and significant figures

en.text: To round, find the rounding digit. Look at the digit to its right. If it is 0 to 4, keep the rounding digit. If it is 5 to 9, add 1. Decimal places count digits after the point. Significant figures count from the first non-zero digit.

am.text: ለማጠጋጋት የማጠጋጊያውን አሃዝ ፈልግ። ከቀኙ ያለውን አሃዝ ተመልከት። 0 እስከ 4 ከሆነ አሃዙን አቆየው። 5 እስከ 9 ከሆነ 1 ጨምር። የአስርዮሽ ቦታዎች ከነጥቡ በኋላ ያሉ አሃዞች ናቸው። ጉልህ አሃዞች ከመጀመሪያው ዜሮ ያልሆነ አሃዝ ይቆጠራሉ።

screens.title: A number in the news
screens.text: A radio report says a town has about 38,700 people. The exact count is 38,721.
screens.ask: Round 45,676 to the nearest 100. Take a guess.
screens.after: It is 45,700. Read on to see the rule.

screens.title: Limit of accuracy
paras: Measuring a child's temperature rarely gives an exact value. So does a dose of medicine, or the area of a field.
So we use approximations.
This part covers rounding, decimal places (d.p.), significant figures (s.f.) and accuracy.

screens.title: Rounding whole numbers
paras: First find the rounding digit. It is the tens digit when rounding to the nearest 10. It is the hundreds digit for the nearest 100, and so on.
Then look at the digit to its right.
If it is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4: keep the rounding digit. All digits to its right become 0.
If it is 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9: add 1 to the rounding digit. All digits to its right become 0.
Example 1. A town has 38,721 people. To the nearest 100 this is 38,700. The digit after 7 is 2, so 7 stays.
To the nearest 1,000 it is 39,000. The digit after 8 is 7, so 8 becomes 9. To the nearest 10,000 it is 40,000.
The rounded numbers are less accurate but easier to use.
screens.note: Correction: the printed book gives 38,721 to the nearest 100 as "36,700" and calls it "rounded up". It is 38,700, and it is rounded down.

screens.title: Name it
defs: Replacing a number by a simpler nearby value. 38,721 → 38,700 to the nearest hundred.

screens.title: Nearest thousand
screens.why: The thousands digit is 5. The next digit is 6, so 5 becomes 6.
screens.clue: Find the thousands digit. Then look at the digit just to its right.

screens.title: Decimal places
paras: To round to a number of decimal places, look at the next digit.
Example 2. (a) 10.673 to 1 d.p.: the second digit is 7 (5 or more). So round up: 10.7.
(b) 3.173 to 2 d.p.: the third digit is 3, so 3.17.
Rounding to 1 d.p. means to the nearest tenth. 2 d.p. means to the nearest hundredth.

screens.title: Significant figures
paras: In 43.25, the 4 is the most significant figure. It is worth 40.
The 5 is the least significant. It is worth 5 hundredths.
Count significant figures from the first non-zero digit.
Example. (a) 2.364 to 2 s.f. is 2.4. (b) 0.0062 to 1 s.f. is 0.006. The leading zeros are not significant.

screens.title: Two ways to state accuracy
defs: A digit after the decimal point. 3.17 is given to 2 decimal places (2 d.p.).
The digits counted from the first non-zero digit. 0.0062 has 2 significant figures.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.why: The first two significant figures are 4 and 0. The next digit is 8, so 0.0408… rounds to 0.041.
screens.clue: Start counting at the first non-zero digit, 4.

screens.title: Two decimal places
screens.why: The third decimal digit is 6, so the 2 becomes 3: 8.43.
screens.clue: Look at the third digit after the point. Is it 5 or more?

screens.title: Market takings
screens.text: Almaz sells teff in Adama market. This month she took 45,676 birr.
screens.ask: She tells her family the amount to 2 significant figures. What does she say?
screens.why: The first two significant figures are 4 and 5. The next digit is 6, so 45 becomes 46.
screens.clue: Count two digits from the left. Then look at the third.
screens.worked: The first two significant figures are 4 and 5. The third digit is 6, which is 5 or more. So 45 becomes 46, and the rest become 0: 46,000 birr.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.why: The first three figures are 2, 8 and 7. The next digit is 9, so 7 becomes 8.
screens.clue: Count three figures from the first non-zero digit, then look at the next one.

en.text: A rounded number hides its real value. The lower and upper bounds show the limits. Halve the accuracy. Subtract the half for the lower bound and add it for the upper bound. When we add, subtract or multiply rounded numbers, the answer is a range too.

am.text: የተጠጋጋ ቁጥር እውነተኛ እሴቱን ይደብቃል። ዝቅተኛና ከፍተኛ ወሰኖች ገደቡን ያሳያሉ። ትክክለኛነቱን ግማሽ አድርግ። ለዝቅተኛው ወሰን ግማሹን ቀንስ፣ ለከፍተኛው ደግሞ ጨምር። የተጠጋጉ ቁጥሮችን ስንደምር፣ ስንቀንስ ወይም ስናባዛ መልሱም ክልል ይሆናል።

screens.title: Which numbers give 3.5?
screens.text: Many numbers round to 3.5 to 1 d.p. Look at 3.42, 3.45, 3.49, 3.54 and 3.57.
screens.ask: What is the smallest of these that rounds to 3.5? Take a guess.
screens.after: It is 3.45. The largest is 3.54. Read on to see why.

screens.title: Accuracy: upper and lower bounds
paras: Definition 1.14. The lower and upper bounds are the limits of the values a number could have had before it was rounded.
1.5, 1.50 and 1.500 look the same. But they are written to different accuracies.
1.5 (to 1 d.p.) could be anything from 1.45 up to, but not including, 1.55 (Figure 1.9).
We write 1.45 ≤ x < 1.55.
1.45 is the lower bound and 1.55 the upper bound.
screens.note: Definition 1.14 says the bounds are "the maximum and minimum values". Strictly, the upper bound itself is not allowed: 1.55 rounds to 1.6, not 1.5. That is why the inequality uses < on the right.

screens.title: The two limits
defs: The smallest value a number could have had before it was rounded.
The value just above the largest it could have had. The number is always less than it.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.text: A length is 8 cm to the nearest cm. Which is its lower bound?
screens.why: Half of 1 cm is 0.5 cm, and 8 − 0.5 = 7.5.

screens.title: Finding the bounds
screens.text: A tree weighs 872 kg to the nearest kg.
steps: Find the place value of the accuracy. Here it is 1 kg.
Example 2. 10.7 to 1 d.p.: half of 0.1 is 0.05. The bounds are 10.65 and 10.75.

screens.title: A lower bound
screens.text: A number is 12.6, correct to 1 d.p.
screens.clue: The accuracy is 0.1. Halve it first.

screens.title: Effect of operations on accuracy
paras: Activity 1.23. a = 5 and b = 2, to the nearest whole number.
Lowest sum: lower + lower = 4.5 + 1.5 = 6. Highest: upper + upper = 5.5 + 2.5 = 8.
For a − b with a = 9 and b = 6: lowest is lower a − upper b = 8.5 − 6.5 = 2. Highest is upper a − lower b = 9.5 − 5.5 = 4.
When rounded numbers are added, subtracted or multiplied, the answer is a range.

screens.title: Example 1: a rectangular farm
paras: A rectangular farm is 12 m long and 6 m wide, to the nearest metre.
(a) Sum: smallest 11.5 + 5.5 = 17.0 m. Largest 12.5 + 6.5 = 19.0 m.
(b) Area: smallest 11.5 × 5.5 = 63.25 m². Largest 12.5 × 6.5 = 81.25 m².
The largest area is found by multiplying the two upper bounds.
screens.note: Correction: Example 1(b) in the printed book says the upper bound of the area "is obtained by adding the two upper bounds" and calls it "the maximum sum". It is found by multiplying them, and it is the maximum area.

screens.title: Check your understanding
screens.text: For a − b, which combination gives the smallest possible answer?
opts: Lower bound of a − upper bound of b
Lower bound of a − lower bound of b
Upper bound of a − upper bound of b
Upper bound of a − lower bound of b
screens.ans: Lower bound of a − upper bound of b
screens.why: Start as small as possible and take away as much as possible.

screens.title: A teff field
screens.text: Abebe's teff field is 20 m long and 10 m wide, each to the nearest metre.
screens.ask: What is the upper bound of its area?
screens.why: The upper bounds are 20.5 m and 10.5 m, and 20.5 × 10.5 = 215.25.
screens.clue: Find the upper bound of each side first. Then use the right operation.
screens.worked: Half of 1 m is 0.5 m. Upper bounds: 20 + 0.5 = 20.5 m and 10 + 0.5 = 10.5 m. Multiply them: 20.5 × 10.5 = 215.25 m².

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: To find the upper bound of an area, multiply the upper bounds of the length and width.
screens.why: The largest possible length times the largest possible width gives the largest area.
screens.clue: Think about the farm example. Which length and width make the biggest farm?

items.ask: 35.946 to the nearest whole number is ___
items.why: The digit after 5 is 9, so 35 becomes 36.
items.clue: Look at the first digit after the point.

items.ask: 45.1999 to the nearest whole number is ___
items.why: The digit after 5 is 1, so 45 stays.
items.clue: Only the first digit after the point matters.

items.ask: 7/8 to the nearest whole number is ___
√5 to the nearest whole number is ___

items.text: Write 1.936 to 1 d.p. and to 2 d.p.
items.why: To 1 d.p. the next digit is 3, so 1.9. To 2 d.p. the next digit is 6, so 1.94.
items.clue: Do each one separately. Look at the digit after the last one you keep.

items.text: Write 12.998 to 1 d.p. and to 2 d.p.
items.why: Both round up through the 9s. The zeros show the accuracy: 13.0 and 13.00.
items.clue: Rounding up a 9 makes a carry. Keep the right number of decimal places.

items.why: The first figure is 2. The next is 8, so 2 becomes 3: 30,000.
items.clue: Keep one figure. Fill the other places with zeros.

items.why: The first three figures are 4, 1, 9. The next is 0, so 41,900.
items.clue: Keep three figures. Look at the fourth.

items.why: The first three figures are 4, 5, 5. The next is 6, so 4.56.
items.clue: Keep three figures. Look at the fourth.

items.text: A car's speed is 45 m/s to the nearest integer. Which inequality gives the range for v?
items.why: Half of 1 is 0.5, so the bounds are 44.5 and 45.5. The upper bound is not included.
items.clue: Halve the accuracy. Which end can v not equal?

items.text: Find the bounds of 12.6, given to 1 d.p.

items.ask: 4.23 is given to 2 d.p. Its lower bound is ___

items.text: Write y = 21.36 as an inequality between its bounds.
items.why: 21.36 is to 2 d.p. Half of 0.01 is 0.005.
items.clue: How many decimal places does 21.36 have?
Count the decimal places, then halve that accuracy.

items.text: Each number is given to 1 d.p. Find the bounds of 5.4 + 6.2.
items.clue: Add the two lower bounds, then the two upper bounds.

items.ask: Each is to 1 d.p. The lower bound of 4.6 × 2.7 is ___

items.text: Each number is given to 1 d.p. Find the bounds of 14.3 − 5.7.
items.clue: For the smallest difference, take as much away as you can.

items.text: Each number is to 1 d.p. Which gives the smallest value of 10.8 ÷ 3.1?
items.why: Smallest = lower ÷ upper ≈ 3.413. Largest = upper ÷ lower ≈ 3.557.
items.clue: A smaller top and a bigger bottom make a smaller answer.

items.ask: A school football field is 102.6 m by 49.5 m, each to 1 d.p. The lower bound of its area is ___ m².
items.clue: Find each lower bound, then multiply.

test.ask: 38,721 rounded to the nearest hundred is ___
test.why: The digit after the hundreds digit is 2, so 7 stays and the rest become 0.

test.text: A mass is 6.4 kg to 1 d.p. What are its bounds?

test.why: Leading zeros are not significant. The first figure is 6, and the next is 2, so 0.006.

notes.text: The printed book gives 38,721 to the nearest 100 as "36,700" and calls it "rounded up". It is 38,700, and it is rounded down.
Definition 1.14 says the bounds are "the maximum and minimum values". Strictly, the upper bound itself is not allowed: 1.55 rounds to 1.6, not 1.5. That is why the inequality uses < on the right.

Example 1(b) in the printed book says the upper bound of the area "is obtained by adding the two upper bounds" and calls it "the maximum sum". It is found by multiplying them, and it is the maximum area.
